name: argument-parser-negative-test-706c373f17/defaultable-too-many-p.bal
spec_references: Module-level declarations: Function definition — Supports `required-params`, `defaultable-params`, `included-record-param` and `rest-param` in the signature
Expressions: Literal — Currently support `nil-literal`, `boolean-literal`, `numeric-literal` and `string-literal` only

Invocations / Named and default arguments: Named arguments and omitted defaultable arguments are supported for function calls when the callee has an atomic function type with a known parameter signature.
reason: The declaration combines supported required/defaultable parameters and string/numeric defaults. However, the actual negative scenario supplies eight command-line strings to a six-parameter public main and expects startup failure. The supplied subset specification covers function signatures and language-level calls, but does not cover command-line binding, entry-point argument conversion, or excess CLI argument rejection. Whole-case classification is therefore feature for this unlisted execution interface, rather than a failure involving unsupported defaultable-parameter syntax.
unsupported_constructs: Command-line argument binding to main and rejection of excess positional command-line arguments are not covered.
test_design_notes: The @args and @panic comments are harness markers; there is no language-level call or panic statement.
The empty body makes failure depend entirely on startup argument handling. The decimal exponent default and multiple primitive parameter types are mixed into the CLI scenario.
No obvious malformed source or migration marker placement problem is visible; the generic @panic marker does not identify the expected diagnostic.
